title: Set Up CI/CD Pipeline with GitHub Actions
description: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs tests, linting, and deploys your capstone project
objective: Students will set up a complete CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions with automated testing, linting, and deployment trigger for their capstone project

steps.title: Initialize Git and Push to GitHub
steps.instructions:
Open your capstone project folder in the terminal.

**Step 1: Initialize Git**
```bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit: FastAPI capstone project"
```

**Step 2: Create a GitHub repository**
1. Go to https://github.com/new
2. Name it `smartattend-capstone` (or your project name)
3. Keep it Public (so GitHub Actions is free)
4. Do NOT add a README (we already have code)
5. Click "Create repository"

**Step 3: Push your code**
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/smartattend-capstone.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```

**Step 4: Create a develop branch**
```bash
git checkout -b develop
git push -u origin develop
```

You should now see your code on GitHub with two branches: `main` and `develop`.

steps.title: Write Your First Test
steps.instructions:
Before setting up CI/CD, we need tests for the pipeline to run.

Install test dependencies:
```bash
pip install pytest pytest-asyncio httpx
```

Create `tests/test_api.py`:

```python
"""Tests for the SmartAttend API."""
import pytest
from httpx import AsyncClient, ASGITransport
from app.main import app


@pytest.fixture
def anyio_backend():
    return "asyncio"


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_health_check():
    """Test that the health endpoint returns 200 OK."""
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app)
    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://test") as client:
        response = await client.get("/api/v1/health")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["status"] == "ok"


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_create_student():
    """Test creating a new student."""
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app)
    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://test") as client:
        response = await client.post("/api/v1/students", json={
            "name": "Test Student",
            "email": "test@example.com",
            "phone": "9876543210",
            "batch": "TEST-2026",
            "city": "Bhopal"
        })
    assert response.status_code == 201
    data = response.json()
    assert data["name"] == "Test Student"
    assert data["email"] == "test@example.com"


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_list_students():
    """Test listing students returns a list."""
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app)
    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://test") as client:
        response = await client.get("/api/v1/students")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert isinstance(response.json(), list)


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_student_not_found():
    """Test that getting a non-existent student returns 404."""
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app)
    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://test") as client:
        response = await client.get("/api/v1/students/99999")
    assert response.status_code == 404


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_invalid_attendance_status():
    """Test that invalid attendance status returns 400."""
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app)
    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://test") as client:
        # First create a student
        await client.post("/api/v1/students", json={
            "name": "Attendance Test",
            "email": "att-test@example.com",
            "batch": "TEST-2026",
            "city": "Delhi"
        })
        # Try invalid status
        response = await client.post("/api/v1/attendance", json={
            "student_id": 1,
            "date": "2026-07-25",
            "status": "invalid_status"
        })
    assert response.status_code == 400
```

Run the tests locally:
```bash
pytest tests/ -v
```

All 5 tests should pass. If any fail, fix the issues before proceeding.

steps.title: Create the GitHub Actions Workflow
steps.instructions:
Create the workflow file:

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
```

Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with this content:

```yaml
name: CI Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    name: Lint & Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python 3.12
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install fastapi uvicorn sqlalchemy[asyncio] aiosqlite pydantic[email] python-dotenv
          pip install pytest pytest-asyncio httpx ruff

      - name: Lint with Ruff
        run: ruff check app/ tests/ || true

      - name: Run tests
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: sqlite+aiosqlite:///./data/test.db
          SECRET_KEY: test-key
        run: |
          mkdir -p data
          pytest tests/ -v

      - name: Run tests with coverage
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: sqlite+aiosqlite:///./data/test.db
          SECRET_KEY: test-key
        run: |
          pip install pytest-cov
          pytest tests/ --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing
```

Save the file. This workflow will:
1. Trigger on every push to `main` or `develop`
2. Trigger on every pull request to `main`
3. Install Python 3.12 and all dependencies
4. Run linting with Ruff
5. Run all tests with pytest
6. Show code coverage report

steps.title: Push and Watch the Pipeline Run
steps.instructions:
Commit and push the workflow:

```bash
git add .github/workflows/ci.yml tests/test_api.py
git commit -m "Add CI pipeline with GitHub Actions and tests"
git push origin develop
```

Now go to your GitHub repository and click the **Actions** tab.

You should see:
1. A workflow run named "CI Pipeline" in progress (yellow dot)
2. Click on it to see the details
3. Click on the "Lint & Test" job to see each step
4. Wait for it to complete (green checkmark = success)

If it fails (red X):
- Click on the failed step to see the error message
- Fix the issue locally
- Commit and push again
- The pipeline will re-run automatically

**Now create a Pull Request:**
1. On GitHub, click "Pull requests" tab
2. Click "New pull request"
3. Set base: `main`, compare: `develop`
4. Click "Create pull request"
5. You should see the CI pipeline running as a check on the PR
6. Wait for it to pass (green checkmark)

The PR should show "All checks have passed" before you merge.

steps.title: Add a Status Badge to Your README
steps.instructions:
Add a CI status badge to your `README.md` so anyone visiting your repo can see if tests are passing.

Open your `README.md` and add this at the very top:

```markdown
# SmartAttend

![CI](https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/smartattend-capstone/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)

> Student Attendance Management System for TechPath Institute, Bhopal
```

Replace `YOUR_USERNAME` with your actual GitHub username.

Now commit and push:
```bash
git add README.md
git commit -m "Add CI badge to README"
git push origin develop
```

Go to your GitHub repo — you should see a green badge that says "CI: passing".

**Verify your complete setup:**
- [ ] GitHub Actions workflow file exists at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- [ ] At least 5 tests in `tests/test_api.py`
- [ ] Pipeline runs on push to `develop` and PR to `main`
- [ ] Latest run shows green checkmark (all tests pass)
- [ ] README has a CI status badge
- [ ] You successfully created and merged a PR with CI checks

Congratulations — you now have a professional CI/CD pipeline! Every time you push code, tests run automatically. This is how real software teams work.

starter_code:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install pytest
      - run: pytest tests/ -v
expected_output: A GitHub repository with a working CI/CD pipeline: .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs on push and PR, at least 5 passing tests visible in the GitHub Actions tab, a green CI badge in the README, and at least one successfully merged pull request with CI checks
